reply.subject: RM_LadderSteel

observed.facings.png: Four lowered facings on one shared scale. South: only two small black inverted-U hooks, set far apart. East: a short, wide rack. Thick doubled horizontal tubes run along its top and bottom, thin vertical rods join them, and the hooks sit at the right ends. North: a tall ladder seen face-on, with two dark tube rails topped by hooked crooks, thin rungs, and stringers that close in toward the bottom. West: the east view mirrored.
observed.south.png: Two dark, rounded inverted-U pipe hooks, each with a small foot, about 130 px apart near the middle of the canvas. Nothing else is drawn. Clean alpha.
observed.east.png: Sits in the lower right of the canvas. Two thick horizontal tube pairs, one at the top and one at the bottom, each pair a guide rail plus a stringer with collars. Four or five thin vertical rods span between them. Hooked crooks curl at the right ends. The top tube rises slightly toward the right and the bottom tube drops slightly, so the frame is wider at the right. Dark steel with grey highlights.
observed.north.png: A face-on ladder. Two outer guide rails with hooked tops curl over at roughly the upper third. The inner stringers start a little above the hooks and close in toward the bottom. There are about eight thin round rungs, and the gaps between them shrink lower down. The rails have collar clamps. Dark gunmetal-black. Open and light, not dense.
observed.west.png: The east view mirrored: hooks at the left ends, tubes running horizontally, thin vertical rods. Sits in the lower left of the canvas.
observed.scale.png: Pit overview beside a vanilla human head. The north ladder stands on the light north wall band, with its hooks over the black rim line and its feet stopping where the dark floor begins. The east and west ladders sit on the narrow side bands, hooks at the outer rim, and stay on the light band. The south view is two hooks on the near rim line. All are thin and dark.
observed.wall_context.png: Left panel, lowered. North ladder on the north band, hooks over the rim, stopping at the band's lower edge. East and west ladders lie horizontal across the side bands, hooks at the outer rim, reaching inward only to the band's edge. South shows two hooks. Right panel, raised. The north ladder is slid up: its top stands about 0.4 cell above the rim, it is still between the guide rails, and the rails continue down the band below it. On the east and west walls the ladder body is shifted outward past the rim onto the surface. The guide-rail tubes stay on the band with flanged ends. The south view shows a short ladder top standing above the near rim between the two hooks.
observed.variants_1.png: Raised north alone. The ladder rises above the hooked guide rails, with about eight rungs. The rails clasp the ladder stringers with collars, and their lower legs continue down with clamp feet. It reads as a slid-up ladder held in its rails.
observed.variants_2.png: Raised east. Thin guide-rail tubes with flanges run left from the hooks. The ladder frame (thick top and bottom tubes, vertical rods) is shifted right relative to the rails and overlaps them over about half its length.
observed.variants_3.png: Raised west: the raised east mirrored.
observed.variants_4.png: Raised south. A short ladder top, four rungs between two stringer posts, stands behind and between the two inverted-U hooks.
observed.variants_5.png: Zoom sheet. North wall: lowered is a clean, fire-escape-style ladder whose rails converge downward and whose rung gaps narrow; raised slides up past the rim and stays held by the rails. East and west walls: lowered lies on the light band, hooks over the rim line, with the long axis horizontal and stopping at the band's inner edge, just short of the dark. Raised shifts the ladder outward over the rim, with the rails left on the band. The stringers have visible tube thickness and collars.

CAMERA.seen: There are no round tops to measure. The north view is face-on and recedes down the sloped band. The side views are the north view turned a quarter and squeezed to the band, matching the pit drawing convention on the card.

BORE.seen: The rail crooks are solid curled tubes. No open pipe bore faces the camera in any view.

PORTS.seen: The card defines no ports, and nothing is coupled to this subject.

WALL_LEAN.seen: In wall_context, the east ladder's hooks sit at the right (outer) rim and it runs left onto the band. West mirrors this, with hooks at the left rim. North hooks sit at the top rim and the ladder runs down. Each facing matches its wall side.

WALL_AXIS.seen: North runs vertically on screen, from the rim down the face. East and west run east-west on screen, from the rim hooks toward the pit centre; the rungs run north-south between the stringers, which is correct.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: No code ports, and no connector-like fittings other than the rail crooks, which are the rail tops described on the card.

LAYERS.seen: No assembled capture is given, and the subject has no attached parts. In wall_context the ladder correctly draws over the rails and rim.

ROTATIONS.seen: The same dark steel tubes, hooked crooks, collars and thin rungs appear in every facing and in both states. The south view is only the rim-top parts, as the description specifies.

SIGNATURE.seen: A ladder on two guide rails whose tops curl over the rim. The lowered and raised states are distinct: the raised ladder is slid up past the rim and still held by the rails.

MATERIAL.seen: Dark gunmetal-black tubes with grey specular highlights and collar clamps read as painted steel, fire-escape black.

FOOTPRINT.seen: The height spread (south 28 px against about 160 px elsewhere) is real by design: south shows only what stands above the near rim. The lowered side views stay inside the light wall band.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-outs on all facings, with no backdrop or cast shadow.

OURS.seen: A custom drawn pipe ladder from draw.py, not vanilla or donor art.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: North is thin, with open rungs and convergent perspective, matching the kept version. The east and west views lie along the band and stop at its inner edge, out of the dark. The raised north is held in its rails. The side-view stringers now have doubled tube thickness instead of wireframe lines.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell the north view reads as a ladder. The side views read as a small dark rail fitting on the wall; less clearly a ladder, but acceptable.

findings.seen: The squeezed side view, with thick horizontal tube pairs and a few thin vertical rods, reads more like a rack or radiator than a ladder at normal zoom. The raised side view, where the ladder is offset from the rails, adds clutter.

findings.fix: The side view shows clearly round rungs spaced evenly between two distinct stringers, with the guide rail visibly behind the stringer, so it reads as a ladder lying down the wall band.

reply.image_seen: 1: four lowered facings on checkerboard; 2: south shows two curled rail tops; 3: east shows a narrow sideways ladder; 4: north shows open rungs between converging rails; 5: west mirrors east; 6: lowered ladders against pit walls beside a human; 7: lowered and raised states composed against all four walls; 8: raised north ladder overlaps two guides extending below it.

concerns.evidence: The raised side views in image 7 show the ladder overlapping two guide tubes, with exposed guide ends extending toward the pit interior. This can correspond to the exposed guides below the raised north ladder, rather than inconsistent construction. However, retaining collars are insufficiently resolved to establish secure attachment. The cited standalone variants_2 and variants_3 are absent.
PORTS is ok: the card specifies no code-defined ports, and the images show no hose, cord or coupler connectors. The curled ends visibly continue the ladder's guide rails.

LAYERS is unreadable, rather than n/a. Image 7 supplies wall compositions, but no identified in-game assembled capture is attached. Actual draw-layer order and wall occlusion therefore cannot be verified; the class module explicitly requires that capture.
